reply.title: The Vertical Throw
reply.story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, stops for the briefest instant at its highest point, and then speeds up as it falls back down. Watching it pause at the top, it is easy to wonder if everything stops completely—including the forces and changes acting on it. Since its velocity is zero at the very top, does its acceleration also drop to zero for that split second?

To find out, we can track the ball's motion from the moment it leaves the hand until it returns. Gravity pulls continuously downward on the ball, changing its velocity at a steady rate throughout the entire flight, whether the ball is moving up, resting at the top, or coming down.
reply.cardDescription: Explore a ball thrown straight up. See how velocity changes while acceleration stays constant at $-g$, even at the peak where velocity is $0$.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed and press Play to watch the motion. Observe how velocity and acceleration behave at the top.
